extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulemakers and staff, environmental regulators, environmental lawyers and advocates (commenters on MACT rulemakings)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal criteria for EPA's eight-year review of MACT (NESHAP) standards, with specific application to glycol dehydrators, storage tanks, and equipment leaks in the oil & gas sector. Focuses on statutory floor-setting, data requirements, consideration of developments, and proper use of available information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect public health and satisfy legal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urge EPA to fully satisfy all legal requirements and protect public health in this important rulemaking for the Oil and Gas Sector, including by considering new science and taking a health-protective approach where there is uncertainty, in order to fulfill the important regulatory duties of CAA §§ 112(f)(2) and 112(d)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is uncertainty EPA should take a health-protective approach; incorporate new science and address each substantive issue raised in comments rather than exempting or weakening the national rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory MACT floor requirements (existing sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard for existing sources must be no less stringent than the emission limitation achieved by the average of the best performing 12 percent of sources in the category (CAA §112(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must calculate the existing-source floor based on the actual emissions profile of the category (average of top 12%); cannot set floors that are less stringent than that average; use representative, reliable data to identify the top performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory MACT floor requirements (new sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard for new sources must be no less stringent than the emission limitation achieved by the best performing source in the category (CAA §112(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must identify the best-controlled similar source and set the new-source floor at that demonstrated level of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review must consider developments in practices, processes, and control technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 112(d)(6) obliges EPA, during the eight-year review, to take into account developments in practices, processes, and control technologies; EPA’s own definition lists: any add-on control technology or other equipment not identified during MACT development; improvements in identified controls that could result in significant additional emission reduction; any work practice or operational procedure not identified; and any process change or pollution prevention alternative that could be broadly applied that was not identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must evaluate these developments and determine whether they warrant revising MACT floors or beyond-the-floor standards; increased acceptance or wider use of a technology is a relevant development that must be considered rather than ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review not limited to narrow 'developments' label
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency’s eight-year review obligation is not statutorily limited to a narrow definition of 'developments' — EPA must assure that MACT standards continue to satisfy substantive requirements of §§112(d)(2)-(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where a technology was considered previously, EPA must determine whether facts underlying earlier assessments have changed and revise limits accordingly; merely noting a technology in the initial record does not excuse reevaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether prior standards were adopted using legally-compliant procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In conducting the review EPA is obliged to 'look back' and ascertain whether the standard was adopted using procedures that comply with the law as it has come to be interpreted by the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior procedures (e.g., choice of data, averaging, statistical methods) were flawed or inconsistent with court decisions, EPA must correct them in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether EPA had sufficiently accurate and comprehensive data originally
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must determine whether it had sufficiently accurate and comprehensive data at the time of the initial standard setting respecting the emissions profile of the category and properly identified the best performing unit(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initial data were incomplete, unrepresentative, or based on limited questionnaires (e.g., asking for a 'representative' unit rather than best-performing units), EPA must seek or use better data (NEI, testing) in the eight-year review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure EPA properly used available data in initial determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must ascertain whether it properly used the available data in establishing MACT floors and standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper uses include relying on control-technology efficiencies rather than plant/unit performance, ignoring better-performing units present in the data set, or not applying statistical methods to identify top performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look around using current data to determine whether emissions profile changed
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must 'look around' with currently available data and determine whether the emissions profile of the industry has changed in a way that would substantially affect the MACT floor calculations, including any increase in the number of good performing units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data such as National Emissions Inventory (NEI), RBLC, state permits and other contemporary sources to evaluate current category performance; do not assume processes unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve data gaps or uncertainties during the review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must determine whether data gaps or uncertainties that affected the earlier decision have been resolved in the interim or can be resolved using new information available to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where information gaps existed in the initial rulemaking, EPA should collect new emissions/testing data or use existing contemporary data sources to close gaps and correct MACT calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider costs and other factors only for beyond-the-floor determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs or other factors may be considered when determining 'beyond-the-floor' MACT standards, but are irrelevant to establishing the MACT floor itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use cost or feasibility to justify a less stringent MACT floor; courts have rejected excluding technologies or limits based on cost when determining the floor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not base MACT floor on control-technologies rather than plant/unit performance
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should not base the MACT floor on an evaluation of control-technology performance rather than plant (unit) performance; MACT floors must reflect the emission level actually achieved by best performing sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must identify top-performing units and base floors on their demonstrated emissions, not just on typical control-device efficiencies reported elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid adopting 'no control' MACT limits without reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must not adopt 'no control' MACT limits (i.e., limits reflecting lack of active controls) where that approach was used previously without reassessing whether circumstances or data have changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If courts have invalidated no-control floors in similar contexts, EPA must revisit and correct prior no-control decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not exclude potential MACT floor technologies because they are not applicable to all sources; subcategorize where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that a particular technology may not be applicable to all sources is irrelevant to whether it should be considered for the MACT floor; EPA can establish subcategories for sources within the performance envelope of a technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a technology (e.g., zero-emission desiccant dehydrators) achieves superior reductions for a subset of sources, EPA should require it for those sources via subcategorization rather than ignoring it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actively consider technologies that could achieve better performance
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must actively 'consider' technologies that could be expected to have better performance than technologies examined in the initial rulemaking and assess whether they warrant revision of floors or standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a technology was previously characterized as 'new' or 'emerging', the eight-year review must evaluate whether it is now commercially demonstrated and broadly applicable enough to affect MACT floors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect updated emissions data when earlier data are outdated
rubrics_metrics.description: Where earlier data (e.g., 1997 survey data) are outdated, EPA should collect new emissions data rather than assuming no significant process change since the older dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: EPA should send updated questionnaires or require testing for small dehydrators; use NEI and other contemporary datasets to reassess category performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document that any numeric alternative meets MACT floor requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must document that any alternate numerical performance standard (e.g., 0.9 Mg/yr benzene) meets MACT floor requirements and is consistent with the statutory floors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing alternate numeric thresholds or averaging options, provide analysis showing they correspond to the average of the top 12% (existing) or best source (new) as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select averaging periods based on best-performing systems' demonstrated performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The averaging period chosen for compliance must reflect the performance of the best performing systems rather than theoretical arguments that favor a less stringent averaging period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should examine actual performance data from top performers to determine appropriate averaging times and show that chosen averaging options meet MACT floor criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate RBLC/BACT/LAER and state/federal requirements as evidence of achievable reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must consider newer regulatory requirements, work practices or emission limitations (including state and local standards, and federal enforcement actions) that are more stringent than the existing §112(d) standard and that demonstrate achievement or achievability of greater reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RBLC/BACT/LAER records (e.g., Michigan Consumer's Energy BACT of 98% efficiency) as part of the fact-finding for the eight-year review.

rubrics_metrics.name: MACT floor calculation should result in significant compliance actions by many sources
rubrics_metrics.description: A properly calculated MACT floor (average of the top 12%) should approximate the performance of about the top 6th percentile performer (for averaging) and thus require a substantial fraction of sources to take steps to comply; if a large majority already meet the proposed floor, the calculation is likely flawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If NEI or other data show that 77% of units already meet the proposed floor, EPA should reexamine the floor calculation and the representativeness of the underlying data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use statistical and testing methods to identify best-performing units (not 'representative' unit reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should not rely on limited questionnaires that ask facilities to report on a 'representative' unit and must instead seek information enabling identification of best performing units (statistically reliable emissions profiles, required testing where needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design surveys and data collection to capture unit-level performance and variability; require emission testing where survey estimates are unreliable or unvalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve contradictions between engineering judgment and available data
rubrics_metrics.description: Where background or engineering documents indicate higher feasible efficiencies (e.g., condenser+combustion can achieve 99%+), EPA must reconcile any contradictory lower floor determinations by resolving data gaps and updating the floor accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If earlier memos state potential control combinations yield higher reductions, EPA should use current evidence to set floors consistent with demonstrated capabilities rather than relying on unsupported conservative assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use absence of 'conclusive' information as a bar to acting on available information
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not barred from acting if information is not 'conclusive'; the Act requires setting MACT floors based on the information available at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where information is limited, EPA still must set floors consistent with best-available data and should pursue additional data in the eight-year review to refine floors rather than leaving standards lenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address exemptions and carryovers from prior standards for continued appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should evaluate exemptions carried over from earlier standards (e.g., exemptions originating in early NSPS) to determine their propriety under current law and their impact on HAP emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not perpetuate exemptions without assessing whether they undermine MACT statutory requirements or current emission-control availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle practical concerns for some facilities on a case-by-case basis, not by weakening national rules
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should not decline to require continuous monitoring or other protective measures across the board because of practical concerns for some facilities; instead it can address such issues on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where some facilities face particular practical issues, EPA may use targeted exemptions, variances, or subcategories rather than weakening the national standard for all sources.
